strategy_objective_guidance:
- Single scored term: `combined_score = (min triangle area over 286 triples) / (ConvexHull area) / 0.030936889034895654`. There is no other component — no runtime penalty, no smoothness term. Runtime only matters as a hard timeout.
- The objective is scale/translation/rotation/affine invariant (both numerator and denominator scale identically under affine maps), so fix a normalization (e.g., hull area = 1) to remove degenerate degrees of freedom.
- The score is a **max-min** problem: the minimum of 286 piecewise-linear area functions is concave-piecewise; it is non-smooth and has many near-equal active triangles at the optimum. The largest lever is raising the *smallest* triangle areas — the active set — not improving average quality.
- Hard validity constraints: return a finite NumPy array of shape (13,2); hull must be non-degenerate (ConvexHull must succeed, hull area > 0). Any exception → score 0. So robustness (always return a valid incumbent) is critical.
- The program receives **no input at all** — the whole task is offline/batch: all computation (long multistart, heavy refinement) can be done at call time within the timeout, or even precomputed offline and embedded as a starting configuration (but not hard-coding evaluator outputs; embedding a good point set as an *initialization* is fine and then improving it).
- No conflict between terms (only one term), but there is an internal tradeoff: pushing hull area down raises the normalized ratio, while interior points that shrink the hull also create small triangles. The optimum balances hull compactness against minimum-triangle size.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- **Nonsmooth max-min via repeated LP/active-set sweeps**: treat the min-area as a linear constraint per active triple and solve small LPs/QPs; scipy.optimize.linprog or scipy.optimize.minimize(method='SLSQP') with constraints on the currently-smallest triangles; scipy.spatial.ConvexHull for the denominator.
- **Smooth-minimum surrogate optimization**: replace min with -1/α·log(Σexp(-α·A_i)) or softminimum with adaptive α; use scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B') with analytic gradients over 26 variables; anneal α upward.
- **Structured/symmetry-templated configurations**: place points on parametrized curves (ellipse boundary points + interior rings, regular polygon perturbations) with few shape parameters; optimize those parameters — drastically fewer variables, deterministic, good for multistart diversity.
- **Stochastic global search, deterministic-seeded**: multistart from scrambled low-discrepancy point sets (numpy.random.Generator with fixed seeds, numpy.random.Sobol) followed by local polish; keep best incumbent.
- **Direct nonsmooth local methods**: scipy.optimize.minimize(method='Nelder-Mead') or Powell on the raw min objective (robust to nonsmoothness), restarted from perturbed incumbents.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Active-set refinement: identify the ~10–30 smallest triangles each iteration, constrain/optimize only those areas, drop constraints whose duals vanish; iterate until the active set stabilizes.
- Adaptive smooth-min temperature: start α ≈ 50·(typical area), increase ×2 every ~100 L-BFGS iterations until α ≈ 10⁵; final polish with Nelder-Mead on the exact min.
- Multistart budget: e.g., 200–1000 deterministic starts (fixed seed), keep global best; per-start iteration caps; total time comfortably under timeout with early exit when no improvement in N rounds.
- Normalization: after each improvement, rescale so hull area = 1 (or centroid at origin) to keep the optimizer in a well-conditioned region; enforce via ConvexHull(points).volume.
- Perturbation schedule: multiplicative Gaussian jitter on the incumbent with decaying σ (e.g., 0.01 → 1e-5 of hull diameter), accept only if exact min-area improves; fully deterministic given the seeded Generator.
- Safety: wrap all optimization in try/except; cache the best valid (13,2) array found so far and return it unconditionally on any failure; validate finiteness with np.isfinite before returning.

strategies.title: [epigraph-active-set] Exact max-min epigraph refinement with active-set constrai
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Epigraph-variable constrained optimization with iterative active-set re-selection (LP/QP-style nonsmooth handling).
Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent's two polish phases inside `heilbronn_convex13()` — the fixed-tau softmin anneal loop and the single-triangle `exact_obj` SLSQP step — with an epigraph formulation applied to the best incumbent and to each multistart result.

This directly attacks the nonsmooth max-min structure: at the true optimum many triangles are exactly equal, and constraint-based equalization is the only mechanism that can raise the whole active band simultaneously, which the incumbent's smooth surrogate and single-active-triangle gradient provably cannot (its gradient only sees one triangle). strategies.title: [template-topology] Parametrized structured templates with few shape variables
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Geometrically distinct deterministic seed topologies optimized over few shape parameters (mesoscopic subsystem replacement of the start generator).
Replacement scope: Replace the `starts` construction block in `heilbronn_convex13()` (the two-ring and random families) with a library of parametrized templates optimized in a low-dimensional shape space before full 26-variable refinement.
Compute budget: ≤ 12 templates × ≤ 8 shape parameters × ≤ 300 L-BFGS-B iterations each (cheap: area function only), plus the existing per-start pipeline on the top 6 template optima; expected total time ≤ 150 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's starts are all two-ring or uniform-random; all its local optima share the same contact topology (outer ring + inner ring), which is a structural ceiling — known good 13-point Heilbronn-type configurations are not two concentric rings. New topologies with genuinely different contact structure: (a) regular 13-gon with per-vertex radial multipliers r_i = 1 + a·cos(4πi/13 + φ) (Fourier-mode ring, 3 params); (b) 4-point square hull + 9 interior points on a 3-lobed rose curve r(θ)=r0(1+b·cos(3θ)) (4 params); (c) two nested regular polygons with independent rotation and a center point, 6+6+1 (3 params); (d) points on an affine image of a triangular lattice patch clipped to the hull (4 params). Optimizing 3–8 shape parameters with L-BFGS-B on the softmin objective is fast and lands in basins the 26-variable SLSQP cannot reach from random starts; each template optimum is then fed to the existing anneal + polish pipeline. Deterministic: all templates closed-form, no RNG. Validity: every template has ≥ 3 non-collinear hull points by construction; final output passes the same finiteness/shape/hull-area checks and incumbent fallback.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the hull/interior contact topology (e.g., rose-curve and lattice-patch interiors versus concentric rings), which the incumbent's start family cannot express at any seed value; falsifiable threshold: if none of the 12 template optima, after full polish, exceeds raw `min_area_normalized` = 0.02138, the strategy is refuted, while any topology whose active triangles distribute over hull edges + lobed interior plausibly reaches ≥ 0.024 (combined_score ≥ 0.78).

strategies.title: [basin-hopping] Deterministic decaying-jitter basin hopping on the exact objecti
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Stochastic global search with decaying perturbation schedule around the incumbent (local-exploitation escape mechanism, distinct from coordinate ascent).
Replacement scope: Replace the final "global incumbent re-polish loop" (the 3-round `_coord_polish` repeat) with a basin-hopping loop seeded from the best incumbent; keep everything upstream unchanged.
Compute budget: ≤ 250 hop iterations, each = one seeded Gaussian perturbation + ≤ 60 Powell iterations on the exact min-area objective + incumbent `_coord_polish`; hard time cap 120 s inside the existing `t_end` guard; expected added evaluation time ~60–90 s, still under the 360 s timeout.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's coordinate ascent moves one point along 4 fixed directions and accepts only strict improvements, so it is trapped in the exact basin of the multistart winner; its re-polish loop provably returns the same point set. Basin hopping applies a multiplicative Gaussian jitter to all 26 coordinates with σ decaying geometrically from 0.01 to 1e-5 of the hull diameter (seeded `np.random.default_rng`, fully deterministic), then re-descends with Powell — a derivative-free method robust to the nonsmooth min — accepting only if the exact `_score` strictly improves. This crosses the ridge lines between adjacent active-set configurations that single-point coordinate moves cannot. Validity: every accepted candidate must have finite coordinates and hull area > 0 (checked via `_hull_area` before acceptance); the pre-loop incumbent is returned unchanged if no hop improves, so the returned array is always a valid (13,2) finite set.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is simultaneous multi-point perturbation with re-descent (hopping between active-set basins), which neither the 4-direction coordinate ascent nor the smooth surrogate can realize; falsifiable threshold: if 250 hops yield zero accepted improvements the strategy is refuted, while historically such schedules on max-min packing problems recover 5–20% of the min-area gap, giving a plausible raw `min_area_normalized` ≥ 0.0225 (combined_score ≥ 0.728) versus the incumbent's 0.02138 / 0.690961.

strategies.title: [lp-steepest-ascent] Exact nonsmooth steepest-ascent direction via per-iteration
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lp-steepest-ascent
Replacement scope: Replace the `_coord_polish` greedy coordinate-ascent phase (and optionally the `exact_obj` SLSQP polish) inside both the main multistart loop and the basin-hopping hop refinement; keep everything else (starts, softmin anneal, incumbent retention) unchanged.
Compute budget: One LP per iteration with ~10–25 active constraints and 26+1 variables via `scipy.optimize.linprog` (HiGHS, microseconds each). Cap at 400 LP iterations per polish call and ~40,000 total LPs across the run; expected evaluation time roughly unchanged (≤ ~200 s) since each LP is far cheaper than a 25-round coordinate polish.
Gain mechanism: The true objective min_i A_i(P)/hull(P) is a concave piecewise-linear function of P on each active-set cell; its steepest-ascent direction is the exact solution of a small LP: maximize t subject to g_k·d ≥ t for every currently-active (near-minimal, within ~1e-9 relative) triangle gradient g_k, with ‖d‖∞ ≤ 1 (the hull-area denominator changes only at second order within a cell, so the numerator direction dominates locally). The incumbent's coordinate ascent explores only 8 axis/diagonal directions per point and its SLSQP exact polish follows a single active triangle's smooth gradient, which stalls whenever ≥2 triangles are simultaneously active — exactly the situation at a max-min optimum, where many triangles tie. The LP direction is the unique correct escape: it raises all tied triangles simultaneously. Step size by exact line search on the true normalized score with backtracking and re-solve of the LP whenever the active set changes (active-set continuation). Wrap in try/except; if linprog fails or returns non-finite, fall back to the existing `_coord_polish`, so the valid incumbent is always preserved.
Expected-gain check: the incumbent's final configurations stall at ties among ≥3 active triangles (its own polish accepts no axis-aligned move there), and the LP direction is by construction a direction along which the exact min-area strictly increases at rate t* > 0 whenever the incumbent is not already at a KKT point of the max-min problem — so any non-KKT incumbent (score 0.955609 < 1.0 reference implies non-optimality) must improve; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 0.955609 after replacing the polish phase.

strategies.title: [phyllotaxis-seeds] Deterministic golden-angle spiral and conic-arc seed familie
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: phyllotaxis-seeds
Replacement scope: Replace the `starts` construction block in `heilbronn_convex13` (the two-ring, radial-jitter, and uniform-random start families) with three new deterministic topologies; the downstream anneal/polish pipeline and incumbent retention stay identical.
Compute budget: ~45 new starts (15 per family) fed into the existing per-start anneal; trim the basin-hopping budget from 150 s to ~120 s to keep total under ~300 s; expected evaluation time similar to the current ~185 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's starts all consist of concentric rings plus uniform noise, so every local optimum it reaches has ring-like contact topology. Three genuinely different deterministic topologies: (a) Vogel/golden-angle phyllotaxis — point k at radius c·√k, angle k·2π(1−φ⁻¹), for c swept over ~6 values, giving a quasirandom, provably well-spread interior with no ring degeneracies; (b) points on a parabola/ellipse arc — parametrize points as (t, t²) for 13 equally spaced t plus affine stretch, the classical Heilbronn construction where triangle areas become a simple quadratic in the parameter gaps, with 3 affine degrees of freedom swept on a small grid; (c) "hexagonal lattice + boundary" — 7 points of a triangular lattice inside a slightly larger hexagon of 6 boundary points, with lattice spacing and hexagon radius as 2 swept parameters. Each family is affine-normalized (centroid at origin, max-norm 1) before entering the existing softmin anneal. New contact topologies (spiral, conic, lattice) access basins the ring starts cannot reach, since the softmin SLSQP is a local optimizer bounded by its start's basin structure. Hard validity: all seeds are finite, distinct, non-collinear by construction (phyllotaxis and lattice points are provably non-collinear for the chosen spacings); the existing finiteness/hull-area guards and best-incumbent return remain untouched.
Expected-gain check: the incumbent's entire multistart portfolio spans only ring-based basins, so any better optimum with spiral/conic/lattice contact topology is unreachable by it; falsifiable threshold: at least one new-seed start, after the unchanged anneal pipeline, yields a normalized min-area strictly above the incumbent's 0.0295636 (combined_score > 0.955609).

strategies.title: [edge-repulsion-moves] Per-point geometric edge-distance repulsion relocation on
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: edge-repulsion-moves
Replacement scope: Insert as a new refinement operator invoked between the softmin anneal and `_coord_polish` for each candidate (and inside basin-hopping hops in place of every other hop's `_coord_polish`); `_coord_polish` itself is kept as the final fallback polisher.
Compute budget: One relocation sweep costs O(13 × active-triangle count); cap at 60 sweeps per candidate with early exit when the normalized score improves by < 1e-12 in a sweep. Expected added evaluation time ≤ 30 s total, offset by halving the basin-hop count.
Gain mechanism: For each point p, collect the triangles containing p whose areas are within a factor 1.5 of the global minimum (the "locally active" set). Each such triangle has an edge opposite p; the triangle's area equals ½·(edge length)·(p's perpendicular distance to the edge line). The incumbent's optimizers move p along global coordinate axes or softmin gradient mixtures, which entangles all 286 triangles; instead, compute for p the exact displacement that maximizes the minimum of its perpendicular distances to the opposite edge lines of its locally active triangles — a 2-D maximin problem solvable in closed form via the Chebyshev-center-style LP of ≤ 3 lines (or by checking the ≤ 6 pairwise-intersection candidates of the offset lines). This is a per-point, geometry-native move: it provably does not decrease any of p's locally active triangle areas (each distance is non-decreasing by construction) while leaving all triangles not containing p exactly unchanged — a monotonicity guarantee the coordinate ascent lacks, which lets it take large safe steps where the incumbent takes none. Iterate points in a deterministic round-robin, re-normalizing by hull area after each sweep. Validity: displacements are clipped to keep the point strictly inside the current hull (hull vertices are moved only inward-projected), all quantities finite, and the best-incumbent guard already in place rejects any regression.
Expected-gain check: at the incumbent's stalled configurations, each active point sits at a local maximin of edge distances only if the current point is already optimal for its active triangles; since the incumbent's polish moves only along 8 fixed directions and provably stalls at multi-triangle ties, the closed-form per-point maximin displacement yields a strictly larger minimum among that point's active triangles whenever the incumbent is not at the per-point optimum — falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 0.955609 on the returned configuration.

A raw-min optimizer is free to (and does) let the hull grow while raising the min area, leaving normalized score on the table — this is exactly the "hull compactness vs min-triangle size" tradeoff the evaluator guide flags. strategies.title: [topology-exchange-moves] Hull/interior membership swaps: push an interior point
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: topology-exchange-moves
Replacement scope: Replace the jitter-only candidate generation in the basin-hopping block of `heilbronn_convex13` (the `sig`-decaying Gaussian hops) with a deterministic schedule of **topology-changing moves**; keep the per-hop fast re-anneal (tau 0.003 → 5e-4) and `_coord_polish` acceptance path unchanged.
Compute budget: ~300 exchange attempts within the existing 165 s hop budget (each attempt = one hull computation + one two-point re-anneal, same cost as a current hop); global 330 s guard retained.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's Gaussian jitter almost surely preserves which points lie on the convex hull, so the search is confined to one boundary/interior topology (one combinatorial class of active triples). The move: (1) pick an interior point q (strictly inside the hull) and a hull vertex v; (2) relocate q to just outside the hull edge midpoint farthest from all other points, and move v inward to the centroid of its two hull neighbors — a swap of hull membership; (3) re-anneal + coordinate polish, accept on strict `_score` improvement. Enumerate all (interior, hull-vertex) pairs deterministically, cycling with a seeded tie-break. This directly changes the contact topology (which triples can be minimal), a degree of freedom no amount of coordinate polishing or jitter can reach. Validity: every candidate is checked for finite coordinates and hull area > 1e-12 before evaluation; incumbent retained on any failure.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the hull-membership partition of the 13 points (incumbent hops cannot cross it because membership is an open condition under small jitter); falsifiable threshold: any accepted swap yielding normalized min-area > 0.030489, with the plausible target being a different topology class whose local optimum exceeds the current 0.030489 basin.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: two-arc-seeds
Replacement scope: Replace the "Family B" parabola block and the uniform-random safety-net starts in `heilbronn_convex13` with a new seed family: 7 points on the upper half of a stretched ellipse, 6 points on a lower shallow parabolic arc, plus an affine-eccentricity sweep; the ring/phyllotaxis/hex families stay.
Compute budget: ~20 new starts replacing ~16 removed ones; per-start cost identical to current (same tau schedule, maxiter 250); expected eval time unchanged (~220 s).
Gain mechanism: The known-good Heilbronn configurations for small n live near convex-curve placements, and the incumbent's single-parabola family forces all 13 points onto one curve where consecutive triples are nearly collinear — the active set is dominated by adjacent triples and the local optimum is structurally limited. Splitting points onto **two** arcs (upper ellipse, lower parabola) makes every small triangle use points from both arcs, so the active set is richer and the achievable min-area is governed by inter-arc separation — a genuinely different contact topology. Construction: for stretch s in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.25} and arc-phase p in {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2}: upper arc points at angles π·(k+p)/(k_max) mapped to the ellipse (s·cosθ, sinθ), k=0..6; lower arc at parameters t=(j+0.5)/6 mapped to (2(t−0.5), −0.6·(1−(2t−1)²) − 0.15); normalize each seed with the existing `_normalize`. Feed through the unchanged anneal + polish pipeline; incumbent fallback untouched.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the two-arc (bipartite active-set) topology, which the single-curve seed families cannot generate because all their points share one curve; falsifiable threshold: at least one two-arc start polishing to normalized min-area > 0.030489, i.e., combined_score > 0.985511.
